subject.title: feat(workspace): add tiered bootstrap loading with configurable bootstrapTier

question: Should OpenClaw accept `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` as a core config/default surface now, and should this PR's no-override legacy behavior plus explicit `minimal`/`standard`/`full` hook-extra semantics be the contract?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the change affects prompt context, session behavior, hook-loaded extras, upgrade expectations, and overlapping bootstrap-control proposals, so automation should not choose the product contract alone.

options.title: Sponsor the linked PR shape
options.body: Proceed with this additive config path after fixing resolver/docs alignment and requiring unchanged no-override defaults plus focused schema, hook, and session coverage.

options.title: Fold into broader bootstrap selection
options.body: Pause this PR behind a broader selector design that covers tiering, per-session filtering, file ordering, and related prompt-pressure issues together.

options.title: Decline the new config knob
options.body: Keep fixed filters and steer users toward existing context injection, bootstrap budgets, lightweight mode, and doctor guidance instead of adding `bootstrapTier`.
